chunks: And Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who had a right against another man, then lost him and did not know where to seek him, and did not know whether he was alive or dead, and did not know any heir, lineage, or child for him, he عليه السلام said: "He should keep searching." He said: "That has gone on for a long time for him, so may he give it in charity?" He said: "He should keep searching."

key_terms.حَقٌّ: a due right or claim owed to another person
key_terms.فَيَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ: to give the amount away as charity
key_terms.وَارِثًا: an heir entitled to inherit or receive the right
key_terms.يَطْلُبُهُ: to seek out the missing person

ai.seo_question: What should be done with money owed to a missing person whose heirs are unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a financial right owed to a missing person whose whereabouts, life status, and heirs are unknown. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام instructs that the person must continue searching and does not permit disposing of the property through charity merely because a long time has passed.
